version: Unversioned. Neither frontmatter has a version field. Both synced files are dated 13 Oct 12:57. motion-video-director/SKILL.md is 508 lines and claymation/SKILL.md is 136 lines. Each skill folder holds only SKILL.md.
purpose: motion-video-director is a local, code-drawn motion-graphics and video-editing director. It renders Canvas/SVG/Three.js/p5.brush/GSAP frames in headless Chrome, encodes them with ffmpeg, and uses faster-whisper, Demucs and cutout models. Its flow is kickoff, preflight, reference intake, then an ElevenLabs VO script that the USER pastes into elevenlabs.io before returning the MP3. After that come storyboard, style board, assets (Freesound/Pixabay/Unsplash/Lottie/Playwright hunting), contact-sheet preview loop, final render and a 15-item QA. It generates no AI images or video, uses no credits, and never calls Hook Lab or Script Lab. claymation is a pure visual-style skill for AI image and video prompts. It offers four locked sub-style blocks, a physicality block, a 12fps stop-motion motion guard and start/end-frame clay transitions. Its image default is Nano Banana 2 and its transition default is Seedance 1.5 Pro. readymerce-animation-ads Phase 8a loads it ("use its blocks word for word"), and it is meant for voiceover + B-roll.

phases.name: Kickoff message (first reply)
phases.does: Read the whole SKILL.md, then send a plain-language explanation of the process, the user's tasks and only the questions still open. Picked from 9 (format, length, vibe, VO yes/no, audience+CTA, brand, personal vs commercial, deadline). Skipped when PROGRESS.md exists: the agent resumes from its 'Next step'.
phases.gate: About 150-250 words plus 3-6 numbered questions, sent once per new project (lines 53, 73). Golden rule (8): 'before your first reply, read this whole SKILL.md from top to bottom'.
phases.human_checkpoint: User answers the questions and names the project folder.

phases.name: Preflight + project scaffold
phases.does: Checks Node ≥18, Python ≥3.10, Playwright+Chromium, ffmpeg/ffprobe, three/gsap/p5/p5.brush, faster-whisper, cutout models, Demucs and the MCPs (LottieFiles, Freesound, Pixabay/Unsplash, Firecrawl, Playwright). Outputs a Tool|Status|Version|Action table. Copies the helper scripts, creates .env with create_env.sh, then builds the folder tree, PROJECT.md, PROGRESS.md, LOG.md and manifest.json.
phases.gate: 'Do not start work until every item is resolved or explicitly skipped' (line 18). Key status is reported as names only, never values.
phases.human_checkpoint: Per-❌ install/skip decisions; user pastes keys into .env and says 'saved'.
phases.tools_models: scripts/preflight.sh, scripts/create_env.sh, scripts/normalize_env.py and scripts/preview.mjs are all referenced. None ships with the skill (see other_issues).

phases.name: References + story intake (+ §13 reference analysis)
phases.does: Collects references, story, audience, platform, length, tone, CTA, brand assets and must-haves. For each reference: ffprobe, 4 fps contact sheets, 10 fps strips around cuts, a spectrogram/transient list and word timestamps, optional Demucs stems. Writes a breakdown and turns it into a recipe.
phases.gate: 'Don't continue until you have at least the story and length' (line 239). 'Analyze max 15 s per reference' (line 433).
phases.human_checkpoint: User confirms the recipe derived from the references (line 437).
phases.tools_models: ffprobe, ffmpeg scene select gt(scene,0.3), faster-whisper, Demucs htdemucs, scripts/analyze_ref.sh (missing)

phases.name: Brief
phases.does: Goal, audience, platform & aspect, length, brand, CTA, references, video type → intensity level (§4, 1 restrained to 5 hyper).
phases.gate: Aspect from the set 9:16 1080×1920 / 16:9 1920×1080 / 1:1 (line 240). Ask only what's missing.

phases.name: VO script for ElevenLabs
phases.does: AV two-column script plus one paste-ready ElevenLabs block (model, voice, settings, export), on-screen keywords list, pronunciation notes, and a variant B hook and CTA.
phases.gate: Word budget by length (15 s 30-38 words ... 90 s 200-220), at 2.3-2.6 words/s with ≈1.5 s end hold. Hook ≤3 s and ≤8 words. Sentences ≤14 words. Tags max 1 per 1-2 lines. CAPS on 1 word per section.
phases.human_checkpoint: **Approve script** (bold gate, line 241). Then the user generates 2-3 takes on elevenlabs.io and returns the MP3 to assets/vo/. 'Steps 3+ (and any scene code) start only after the MP3 arrives.'
phases.tools_models: Eleven v4 (or v3); Multilingual v2 for long reads/PVCs; user-operated web UI, no API call

phases.name: Storyboard / shot list
phases.does: Per shot: time, VO line, visual, motion, transition, SFX and on-screen text. A beat sheet in seconds, written to plan/storyboard.md and plan/shotlist.md (text, not images).
phases.gate: Director rules: one idea per shot, on-screen text ≤6-8 words, reading time ≈0.3 s/word + 0.5 s, reels cut every 0.5-2 s.

phases.name: Style board + font research
phases.does: Palette (hex + roles). Font research → shortlist of 2-3 per role → download from official pages with the licence saved. Type specimen, plus 3-4 still frames rendered from code into plan/styleboard.png.
phases.gate: Max 2-3 families (§12), max 2 typefaces + 1 script accent (line 319). Font licence must be verified.
phases.tools_models: Playwright MCP / Firecrawl for fonts; code-rendered stills (no image model)

phases.name: Assets + VO intake
phases.does: VO intake: ffprobe, volumedetect/ebur128 clipping/loudness check, faster-whisper word timestamps, transcript diff vs the approved script, beats.json locked to the real audio. Then stock, Lottie, SFX and Playwright hunting (§16), cutout mattes, and manifest entries.
phases.gate: Transcript diff clean or a regenerated line requested. Playwright downloads ≤ ~30 per session. Reference-only assets never go into the final without user OK.
phases.human_checkpoint: User regenerates bad lines (vo_lineNN_fix.mp3). User approves the asset contact sheet before anything is used in a final render (§16 step 7).
phases.tools_models: ffprobe, ffmpeg ebur128, faster-whisper, Freesound/Pixabay/Unsplash REST or MCP, LottieFiles MCP, Playwright MCP, RVM/rembg/SAM2-tiny

phases.name: Fast preview loop + preview
phases.does: After every change, node scripts/preview.mjs <from> <to> renders every frame of the range and tiles it into a timestamped contact sheet. --mp4 gives a low-res clip with mixed audio. Before the final, sheets cover the whole video in 10 s chunks.
phases.gate: Defaults 8 fps, 0.25 scale, 6 columns. One loop under ~20 s. Checks framing/safe area, overlaps, legibility, easing gaps, pops/flicker and continuity.
phases.human_checkpoint: **Approve preview** (bold gate, line 245). Golden rule (3): explicit approval before rendering any video.

phases.name: Final render + delivery
phases.does: Full-res deterministic render piped to ffmpeg, then sound mix, loudness and the §15 QA. Output is versioned in renders/final with a render log in renders/logs. Vertical versions are native re-layouts.
phases.gate: ffmpeg -r 30 libx264 yuv420p crf 18. -14 LUFS / TP ≤ -1.5 dBTP (two-pass loudnorm, LRA 11). H.264 yuv420p, AAC 48 kHz, faststart. All 15 QA boxes ticked.
phases.human_checkpoint: Delivery; cleanup offer (move cache to trash)
phases.tools_models: headless Chrome via Playwright, ffmpeg loudnorm

phases.name: QA checklist (15 items)
phases.does: 1) plan and preview approved; 2) hook ≤3 s, CTA ≥2 s; 3) VO is the final MP3 and the transcript diff is clean; 4) captions correct, in safe zones, contrast ≥4.5:1; 5) SFX ±1 frame, VO intelligible, -14 LUFS/-1.5 dBTP; 6) no halos/flicker/dropped frames, ffprobe duration/fps/res correct; 7) H.264 yuv420p AAC 48 kHz faststart; 8) contact sheets over the full duration; 9) manifest licences complete, LOG updated, new version; 10) font licences saved and credited; 11) render log saved and linked, docs current; 12) no API keys anywhere; 13) other aspect versions are native re-layouts; 14) PROGRESS.md Phase: DONE; 15) offer cleanup.

phases.name: Pick one sub-style
phases.does: The user picks 1 = Goofy, 2 = Clean simple, 3 = Stop-motion puppet or 4 = Premium studio plasticine, or describes a custom lane built from the clay fundamentals.
phases.gate: One sub-style per video. Its locked style block opens every image and video prompt verbatim.
phases.human_checkpoint: User picks the style by number (line 39-41)

phases.name: Start frames / references (image prompts)
phases.does: Style block first, then the scene with clay woven into every object, an explicit palette, the camera inside the world at a named angle and the hero product ref attached. Physicality block last.
phases.gate: No 'smooth/polished/glossy'. Visible making-marks, real cast shadows, no set edges or workbench.
phases.tools_models: Nano Banana 2 default; GPT Image 2 fallback; Seedream 4.5 for very creative briefs; reroll on Nano Banana 2 before rewriting

phases.name: Clip prompts (motion)
phases.does: Every clip prompt carries the motion guard (12fps stepped stop-motion, no motion blur, Non CGI, Non cartoon, animation starts at first frame). One motion action per clip.
phases.gate: One gesture, one camera move per in-scene beat.

phases.name: Clay transitions (start/end frame pairs)
phases.does: Builds frame A and frame B around one shared anchor (same refs, end frame referenced from the start frame), with one physical action as the bridge. Camera-bridge or world-bridge (melt, knead, roll-into-ball, coil build-up, smear wipe, hand-of-god, carrier blob). End frame is chained to the next start frame.
phases.gate: Same anchor at similar position and scale. Bridge is one action, 'two or three storyboard drawings'. Nothing silently disappears. Transition prompt = bridge + motion guard only.
phases.tools_models: Seedance 1.5 Pro default for start/end transition clips; refers to a 'first-last-frame' skill that does not exist

story_structures.name: Director spine: Hook → Problem → Solution → Proof → CTA (line 266)
story_structures.shape: Hook 0-3 s (bold claim / pattern interrupt / question / result-first / visual surprise; no logo intro) → Problem → Solution (features as outcomes) → Proof (real UI, numbers, testimonials, before/after) → CTA (one action, shown + spoken, ≥2 s)
story_structures.organic_fit: This works as the POV buyer story for an Albanian marketing agency. The hook is the owner's pain moment (≤8 words, e.g. a post with 3 likes). Problem is a day of posting with no leads. Solution is the agency's mechanism revealed as the turn. Proof is real dashboards and client post screenshots floating in as cards ('Simplify UI ... rather than invent it'). The CTA becomes 'comment PLAN' / save / follow instead of buy or link. Drop the offer and price, and keep the logo only as a ~1.5 s end hold.

story_structures.name: Premium talking-head caption reel (recipe A)
story_structures.shape: Subject walks toward camera; new location every ~3 s with hard cuts on sentence starts → 1-3 word captions around the subject (thin filler + gradient keyword) → counter roll 38→48→50 with photo cards popping in an arc → social-post screenshot as tilted 3D proof plane → pill buttons growing on spoken words → before/after cards → frame-blend ghost whip between takes
story_structures.organic_fit: Agency founder teaching one lesson ('2 things every Tirana business gets wrong on Instagram'). The counter roll shows real client growth, pills name the two things, and post screenshots are the proof. It needs real founder footage. Intensity 3-4. CTA is 'follow for part 2' or 'comment 2THINGS' for the DM funnel. No price.

story_structures.name: Cinematic storyteller documentary edit (recipe B)
story_structures.shape: 1-2 s per visual idea, every sentence a new world, 1-frame black cuts: dim talking head → halftone paper + selection-box word → word-by-word build → torn-paper window to footage → 3D words in the room → dream collage with marker words → 3D picture frame 'At 17' → grunge paper 'OBSESSED' → RGB glitch → hyperspace tunnel chrome word → B&W archival → whip back to A-roll
story_structures.organic_fit: Founder origin story, or a client transformation told as a mini-documentary. Strong for saves and shares and for building affinity. Its intensity 5 clashes with the skill's own 'Corporate / B2B ... 1 – restrained' row, so an agency would run a toned-down version. The organic CTA is 'save this' or 'follow to see the next chapter'.

story_structures.name: SaaS product launch, Slack-style (recipe C)
story_structures.shape: Calm canvas + scramble-decoded tagline → brand orbs condense into app icons in a dock → motion-blur tilt → macro push into dock → cursor hover/click → product UI windows fly out as 3D cards → 3D monitor flattens to line art, push-through → problem line 'Your team lives in too many tools' → giant 'Zero' → 'Zero Alignment' → word swap 'Zero Momentum' → logo overshoot, tracking collapse
story_structures.organic_fit: Mechanism reveal for a service: scattered tools and freelancers condense into one content system. The 'Zero Alignment → Zero Momentum' word swap is the pain beat, and the logo arrives late with no offer. The CTA is 'comment SYSTEM and I'll send the checklist' (keyword funnel).

story_structures.name: Brand-agency kinetic promo, Frontify concept (recipe D)
story_structures.shape: Music only, no VO: 'Your' with orange echo → 'Your Branding is' builds → 'Messy' over dimmed grid of work → card snake along a bezier arc → outline logo draw-on → wordmark over photo → card stack shuffles every beat (~0.31 s) → explodes into 4×2 grid → zoom into a label → search-bar typing → click 'Search' → invert → reveal 'Explore Templates'
story_structures.organic_fit: The closest native fit for a marketing agency: 'Your marketing is Messy' → a snake of the client's random posts → a grid that becomes an organized content calendar → reveal of the agency's system. Being music-only, it works muted and across languages. On-screen text stays ≤6-8 words, and the end card says 'Save this' or 'Comment GRID'.

story_structures.name: Mystery-reveal VO pattern (§10a example)
story_structures.shape: Provocative claim ('Nobody drew this.') → negation ('Not one line… not one frame.') → question ('So where did it come from?') → reveal → CTA line
story_structures.organic_fit: A curiosity loop for organic reels: 'Nobody on this team wrote this post.' → how the system works → 'Follow to see how'. The example's em dashes and 'link below' CTA need replacing for organic and house-style rules.

story_structures.name: Educational / tutorial treatment (§4 intensity 3)
story_structures.shape: Highlights, arrows, step counters, diagrams, calm music; avoid effects that cover content
story_structures.organic_fit: A '3 steps' how-to reel for saves, e.g. '3 things to fix on your Instagram bio'. Step counters drive retention, and the CTA is 'save for later' or 'send to your partner'.

story_structures.name: Clay world-bridge chain (carrier element / hand-of-god / build-up reveal)
story_structures.shape: Start frame A with a shared anchor → one physical action bridge (melt into a plasticine pool, knead and reshape, roll into a ball and unfold, coils assemble the object, clay smear wipe, a real hand re-sculpts one object into another, a recurring clay blob flows scene to scene) → end frame B; end frame chained into the next start frame
story_structures.organic_fit: A POV day in the life of an Albanian shop owner as a clay puppet (sub-style 3, 'story-driven'), with her phone as the anchor and a carrier blob linking scenes: the morning post flops, DMs go unanswered, she tries to boost alone. The revelation of the mechanism is a hand-of-god beat where real hands re-sculpt the chaos into an organized content plan (a coil build-up reveal). The end frame says 'Follow for episode 2' or 'Comment CLAY'. Since there is no product, the anchor is the phone or the content calendar, not a hero product ref.

story_structures.name: Clay camera-bridge reveal
story_structures.shape: Anchor fixed; camera push-in from mid shot to macro on the anchor, or pull-back reveal into a new scene
story_structures.organic_fit: Reveal beats: pull back from one lonely clay 'like' heart to a full clay crowd of customers, or push in on the phone screen to enter the next scene. These are cheap transitions inside an organic story.

story_structures.name: Four clay sub-styles as series treatments
story_structures.shape: 1 Goofy (comedic, high-energy hooks) / 2 Clean simple (calm explainers) / 3 Stop-motion puppet (story-driven, cinematic) / 4 Premium plasticine (sophisticated default); one per video, block verbatim
story_structures.organic_fit: Lock one sub-style per recurring series so the feed is recognisable: puppet for the POV buyer saga, goofy for meme-style hook posts, premium for brand-safe agency explainers. Character identity is held through hero references across episodes.

story_structures.name: Clay shot vocabulary
story_structures.shape: Macro texture close-up · worm's-eye miniature · tilt-shift tabletop · fingerprint insert · clay-frame POV (through a sculpted mirror/window/arch) · googly-eye ECU · hand-of-god cameo
story_structures.organic_fit: Clay-frame POV carries the 'buyer's eyes' framing, and the hand-of-god cameo is a ready metaphor for 'the agency steps in'. A worm's-eye miniature can make the problem feel giant in the pain section.
